_readme: Product marketing framework, v2 range schema (owner, 19 Nov 2026). Platinum Smart-Heat® Electric and Platinum Electric Marine, with the standard and low-clearance recess kits. Matrix 1: what matters to each buyer across twelve benefit fields (w: 3 matters most, 2 matters, 1 nice to have) and the claim that lands. Matrix 2: Platinum Electric against Tungsten Smart-Heat® Electric Series II, so sales know when to sell which. Matrix 3: against Infratech, Heatscope and Heatstrip (factual, sourced, needs_approval Specification and compliance). Product facts come from product-facts.json, bromic.com (read through the fetch tool, 29 Oct and 19 Nov 2026) and Bromic's own manuals and cut sheet on pim.bromic.com and bromic.com (read 19 Nov 2026). Claims add no facts.
name: Platinum Smart-Heat® Electric

launch.summary: Bromic's glass-faced electric heater: a 2.1 in slim body behind a tinted glass-ceramic face, recessed flush or mounted on a wall, ceiling or pole, in black or white, with a 316 Marine version for the coast and the water. It sits above Tungsten Electric for design-led homes, architects, hospitality and yachts.

m2_label.intro: When to sell which: Tungsten Series II on the left, Platinum Electric on the right, benefit by benefit, and the line that tells the buyer why.

m2.s1: Powder-coated body about 183 mm (7.2 in) wide (launch deck); black, white or graphite; Diamond front standard, oval and triangle sold separately; single post, no visible junction box.
m2.s2: Tinted glass-ceramic face in a 304 (or 316) stainless body, 54 mm (2.1 in) deep and 182 mm wide (257 mm on 4500 W); black or white.
m2.so_what: Sell Platinum when the heater must disappear into the architecture; sell Tungsten when the client wants a designed object with a pattern and a colour.

m2.s1: Low-clearance kit (Select and Coastal): 7.5 in minimum cavity, dual cooling fans, recess box supplied, up to 6 kW recessed.
m2.s2: Low-clearance kit: 180 mm (7.1 in) minimum cavity, one integrated cooling fan, recess box supplied, thermal cut-offs, up to 4.5 kW recessed; standard kit needs 10 in (13.8 in for 4500 W).
m2.so_what: Both recess with no site-built box. Platinum fits the shallower cavity with a glass face; Tungsten recesses more power, up to 6 kW.

m2.s1: Open fascia over quartz-sheathed elements, so the glow is visible.
m2.s2: Tinted glass-ceramic fascia that "minimizes light emission" (bromic.com). [[VERIFY: a measured visible-light figure for both — Product team]]
m2.so_what: For a dining room or a yacht at night where light matters, Platinum keeps the glow down.

m2.s1: 2, 3, 4 and 6 kW; coverage up to 65, 100, 130 and 160 ft²; dual elements on 4 and 6 kW; 208, 240 and 277 V.
m2.s2: 2300, 3400 and 4500 W; heat area 65, 108 and 143 ft²; two elements (1.5 and 3 kW) on 4500 W; 208 and 220–240 V, no 277 V.
m2.so_what: Tungsten for the most heat a heater and for 277 V commercial supplies; Platinum for up to 143 ft² with the quieter look.

m2.s1: Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off and Dimmer, manual wall switch, app schedules and timers, Alexa and Google Assistant.
m2.s2: The same Affinity Smart-Heat® Controls; the Dimmer lists Platinum Electric as compatible; 0–100% output in 1% steps.
m2.so_what: One app and one controller family across both, so mixing them on a project is simple.

m2.s1: Ceiling, pitched-ceiling adaptor (3/12 to 12/12, launch deck), wall bracket, cantilevered wall-mount adaptor, single post, tilt up to 45°. [[VERIFY: 30° for 4 and 6 kW in the manual — Product team]]
m2.s2: Wall straight or angled (28–30°), ceiling, 8 in pole included, 2 ft and 4 ft poles, standard or low-clearance recess.
m2.so_what: Vaulted ceilings and steep angles favour Tungsten; flat soffits and clean ceilings favour Platinum.

m2.s1: Coastal: 316 marine-grade stainless with a high-temperature corrosion-resistant coating, IPX5, 316 recess kit; not for marine craft. Select is IPX5.
m2.s2: Marine: AISI 316 stainless, IPX5 (IP55 on 4500 W), Lloyd's Register approval for marine applications, 316 recess kits, warranty 3 years on vessels. Standard: IPX4 or IP54. [[VERIFY: the manuals say the marine heater shall NOT be installed on marine craft — Product team]]
m2.so_what: On a yacht or a cruise ship, Platinum Marine is the Bromic answer; for a home by the sea, both Coastal and Marine fit.

m2.s1: Intertek ETL / cETL; wall 71–72 in, ceiling 96 in, recessed 94 in; fans in the low-clearance kit.
m2.s2: Intertek ETL / cETL 5001799; wall 72 in, ceiling 96 in, recessed about 8 ft (2400 mm); fan and two thermal cut-offs in the low-clearance kit.
m2.so_what: Both are listed electric heat with set clearances; the conversation is about the look and the space.

m2.s1: Revit and CAD files, design service, Partner Program; Series II families at launch.
m2.s2: Revit (ceiling and wall) and CAD files for Platinum Electric, design service, Partner Program.
m2.so_what: Both are ready to specify; Platinum's files are already in the library.

m2.s1: Series II: 3 years on the heater, 7 years on the elements (owner, 22 Nov 2026).
m2.s2: 3 years; Marine 5 years on land and 3 years on vessels (bromic.com).
m2.so_what: Matched cover on land; Platinum Marine adds the longest term in the range.

m2.s1: Black, white and graphite; Diamond, oval and triangle fronts; Classic, Select and Coastal tiers.
m2.s2: Black or white glass; three lengths; Classic and Marine grades.
m2.so_what: More looks to choose from in Tungsten; one refined look, done well, in Platinum.

m2.s1: Recess box supplied with the low-clearance kit; fans on an always-on supply under 1 A; familiar brackets and single post.
m2.s2: Recess box supplied with the low-clearance kit; one fan on an always-on supply under 1 A; bracket and 8 in pole included.
m2.so_what: The same install logic, so a crew that fits one fits the other.

m2_price_note: Directional list prices: Tungsten Series II $643–$1,321 by tier; Platinum Electric $1,527–$2,936; Platinum Marine $3,645–$5,873. Never in ads.

m3.intro: Platinum Electric against the closest glass-faced, slim and recessed electric heaters in the US, Europe and Australia.

competitors.name: Infratech C/CD and W/WD Series
competitors.why_closest: The US benchmark for hardwired electric infrared in premium homes and restaurants, sold through the same dealers and designers, with flush frames for recessing up to 6 kW. The heater architects most often name against Platinum.

competitors.name: Heatscope Vision and Pure+
competitors.owner: MAD Design Group (spec sheets); made in Germany (brochure)
competitors.why_closest: The nearest form factor: slim linear electric heaters with a glass-ceramic front that reduces visible light, in black or white, at a similar premium price, sold to the same design-led buyers.

competitors.name: Heatstrip Elegance
competitors.why_closest: In Australia, the slim, low-light electric heater most often set against Platinum in alfresco ceilings, with its own flush-mount enclosure.

rows.bromic: Tinted glass-ceramic face in 304 or 316 stainless, 54 mm (2.1 in) deep, black or white. Not the thinnest on the market: Heatstrip Elegance is 48.5 mm.

vs.infratech: Quartz element behind a polished stainless reflector and wire guard; colour powder coat on the end caps and housing, the reflector and guard stay stainless; junction box on top of the heater.
vs.heatscope: Glass-ceramic front in black or white; Vision and Pure+ are 87 mm (3.4 in) deep; Pure+ also offers a grill screen.
vs.heatstrip: Coated aluminium body, 48.5 mm deep, in an "off-white" made to blend with white ceilings (2022 overview); no glass face.

RES.claim: A glass face, not a grille: the cleanest-looking heater you can put over the table.

ARC.claim: Glass-ceramic face at 54 mm deep, against a visible reflector and guard on Infratech and an 87 mm body on Heatscope.

DES.claim: Black or white glass with nothing exposed, where Infratech shows its reflector and guard.

BLD.claim: A slimmer glass-faced heater than Heatscope, with no junction box on show.

COM.claim: The look of glass, not hardware, over the guests.

MAR.claim: Glass in 316 stainless, at home in a yacht interior.

rows.bromic: Low-clearance kit: 180 mm (7.1 in) minimum cavity, recess box supplied, integrated cooling fan, two thermal cut-offs, up to 4500 W, 304 or 316; ceiling gradient up to 1/4 in per inch. [[VERIFY: that the kit needs no fire-rated lining under its listing — Product team]]

vs.infratech: W/WD flush frame in a framed pocket "MIN. 2 x 8", lined on all five sides with 5/8 in Type X drywall, "ONLY to be used on a flat non-sloped ceiling"; "After 4 hours of continuous use, a 15 minute cool down period is recommended"; recesses up to 6,000 W.
vs.heatscope: Vision: optional Lift Box and Lift Frame for flush ceiling installation [[VERIFY: depth and listing — Specification and compliance]]; Pure+: no recess kit listed.
vs.heatstrip: Flush Mount Enclosure, powder-coated steel, 125 mm deep with 50 mm clearance behind (about 175 mm in all), up to 3600 W.

RES.claim: Flush with a cooling fan built in, so you can enjoy the whole evening with no cool-down advice.

ARC.claim: 7.1 in cavity with the box supplied and fan-cooled, against Infratech's five-sided Type X pocket on flat ceilings only. Heatstrip's AU enclosure is a little shallower.

DES.claim: A flush glass face in a stainless trim, where Heatscope's Pure+ lists no recess option.

BLD.claim: No framed, drywall-lined pocket to build: the kit is the box. Infratech recesses more power, up to 6 kW.

COM.claim: Flush heat in a shallow canopy, with no cool-down advice on the documents.

MAR.claim: A 316 low-clearance kit for the deckhead; no marine recess option found for Heatscope or Heatstrip.

rows.bromic: Tinted glass-ceramic fascia that minimises light emission (bromic.com); no lumen figure published. [[VERIFY: measured visible light per model — Product team]]

vs.infratech: Medium-wave elements with "a soft, warm glow that is practically unnoticeable" (FAQ).
vs.heatscope: Pure+: 300–600 lm visible light; Vision: 300 lm, "Very discreet filtered ambient light behind a technical glass ceramics screen".
vs.heatstrip: No light figure published; the overview stresses the off-white body that blends with the ceiling.

RES.claim: Warmth with very little glow, so your lighting stays the way you planned it.

ARC.claim: Tinted glass-ceramic face that minimises light emission; ask for a lumen figure before comparing.

DES.claim: A heater that does not light the room, so the lighting designer's scheme holds.

BLD.claim: Discreet heat, with no bright tube on show.

COM.claim: No red glare across the dining room.

MAR.claim: A calm deck at night, with the view, not the heater, in sight.

rows.bromic: 2300, 3400 and 4500 W; heat area 65, 108 and 143 ft² (approximate, varies with model, height and site); 4500 W has 1.5 and 3 kW elements.

vs.infratech: 1.5 to 6 kW in 120–480 V models; chart gives about 121 ft² for the 6,000 W CD at 8–12 ft and 100 ft² for the 4,000 W C.
vs.heatscope: Pure+ 3000 W and Vision 3200 W at 220–240 V, two levels (50% and 100%); no ft² coverage on the product pages.
vs.heatstrip: 1800, 2400 and 3600 W at 240 V; Thermofilm advises 500 W/m² for protected outdoor areas.

RES.claim: Up to 4500 W from one slim glass heater, warming up to 143 ft².

ARC.claim: Above Heatscope's 3.2 kW and Heatstrip's 3.6 kW a heater; Infratech goes to 6 kW. Coverage claims are measured differently by each maker.

DES.claim: More warmth from a glass-faced heater than Heatscope offers.

BLD.claim: Three sizes at 208 or 240 V; for 277 V or 6 kW, use Tungsten Series II or compare Infratech.

COM.claim: 4500 W with staged elements, the most output among the glass-faced heaters compared.

MAR.claim: The full 4500 W also in the 316 Marine version.

rows.bromic: Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off and Dimmer (1% steps), app zones, schedules and timers, Alexa and Google Assistant, 0–10 V and Ethernet to BMS through the expansion board. Controllers sold separately.

vs.infratech: Bond Smart Dimmer with the Universal Control Panel (dimming, timing, zoning) or Smart Switch (on/off, built-in 2-hour timer); Lutron and Crestron through home systems.
vs.heatscope: Two levels, 50% and 100%; remote or external control; optional ZigBee bridge, switch and motion sensor with Alexa and Google Assistant.
vs.heatstrip: Thermofilm recommends its TT-MTM timer controller with temperature control.

RES.claim: Dim in 1% steps from your phone, where Heatscope offers two levels.

ARC.claim: 1% dimming, zones, schedules and BMS integration from one Bromic controller family.

DES.claim: Fine control of the warmth to match the mood of the evening.

BLD.claim: One app and one controller family for every Bromic electric heater on the job.

COM.claim: Zones and schedules per section, with dimming that Heatscope and Heatstrip do not match.

MAR.claim: Integrates with the vessel's systems through 0–10 V or Ethernet.

rows.bromic: Wall straight or angled (28–30°), ceiling, 8 in pole included, 2 ft and 4 ft poles, standard or low-clearance recess; low-clearance kit on gradients up to 1/4 in per inch.

vs.infratech: Wall, ceiling, flush, pole and drop pole; flush frame on flat ceilings only.
vs.heatscope: Wall or ceiling with two screws, extension rods of 100, 300 and 500 mm; Vision lift system and flush Lift Frame; Pure+ horizontal or vertical.
vs.heatstrip: Ceiling, wall, beam, fixed umbrella, recess, chain and rigid poles.

RES.claim: Wall, ceiling, pole or flush: Platinum fits the space you have.

ARC.claim: Recesses on a gentle slope, where Infratech's flush frame needs a flat ceiling.

DES.claim: Drop poles for high rooms, flush for low ones.

BLD.claim: Pole and bracket in the box; longer poles and two recess kits as options.

COM.claim: Fits beams, canopies and soffits across a venue.

rows.bromic: Marine: AISI 316, IPX5 (IP55 on 4500 W), Lloyd's Register approval for marine applications, 316 recess kits. Standard: 304, IPX4 or IP54, for covered spaces.

vs.infratech: 316 stainless as a Marine UpGrade at extra cost on C/CD, W/WD and flush frames; IPX4 on all fixtures (FAQ).
vs.heatscope: Pure+ IP65 "fully exposed outdoor environments"; Vision IP24 in the US brochure, for well-covered spaces; no marine version found.
vs.heatstrip: IP55, high-temperature coated aluminium, described as corrosion-resistant; no marine approval found.

RES.claim: For a home by the sea, a dedicated 316 Marine version, rated IPX5.

ARC.claim: Specify Marine for salt air. For a fully exposed position, Heatscope Pure+ publishes IP65; Platinum belongs under cover.

DES.claim: The same glass look in a marine-grade body.

BLD.claim: 316 heater and 316 recess kit as a range, against an upgrade option on Infratech.

COM.claim: Waterfront venues get a marine-grade heater with a published IPX5 rating.

MAR.claim: Lloyd's Register approval and installs on superyachts and cruise ships: no marine approval found for the others.

rows.bromic: Intertek ETL / cETL 5001799; fixed mounting heights; low-clearance kit with fan and two thermal cut-offs.

vs.infratech: UL and cUL listed, IPX4; flush frame cool-down recommended after 4 hours.
vs.heatscope: "UL approved" for Vision (US brochure); Pure UL pending in 2020 [[VERIFY: current Pure+ listing — Specification and compliance]].
vs.heatstrip: Australian and New Zealand approvals; recommends a timer controller.

RES.claim: Listed, flame-free heat with a fan-cooled recess kit.

ARC.claim: ETL / cETL listed; thermal cut-offs in the low-clearance kit.

DES.claim: Safe, listed electric heat in a furnished room.

BLD.claim: Two thermal cut-offs in the recess kit for peace of mind on every install.

COM.claim: Listed heaters and app timers that switch heat off when service ends.

battlecard.objection: Infratech is what my architect always specifies.
battlecard.answer: Platinum recesses in a 7.1 in cavity with the box supplied and a cooling fan built in, where Infratech's flush frame needs a five-sided Type X pocket on a flat ceiling, and it shows glass, not a reflector and guard.

battlecard.objection: Heatscope also has a glass front and costs about the same.
battlecard.answer: Platinum dims in 1% steps with Affinity controls, goes to 4500 W, carries a 3-year warranty and has a fan-cooled low-clearance recess kit; Heatscope offers two heat levels and no recess kit for Pure+.
Platinum's 4500 W warms up to 143 ft². Where you need 6 kW or 277 V, Tungsten Smart-Heat® Electric Series II is the Bromic choice.

battlecard.objection: The patio is open to the weather.
battlecard.answer: Standard Platinum is made for covered spaces; for salt air choose Marine (IPX5). For a fully exposed spot, ask us for a design plan.

battlecard.objection: I want it to match my black-framed windows.
battlecard.answer: Black glass in a stainless body, with black vent covers on the recess kit.

battlecard.objection: Our ceiling is only 7 inches deep.
battlecard.answer: The low-clearance kit needs 7.1 in from the recess box to the ceiling surface. Send us the section and we will confirm the detail. [[VERIFY: tolerance and options below 7.1 in — Product team]]
